subject: Plotting on only 'half the circle' using coord_polar

messages.author: abd09b73caf0c639
messages.subject: Plotting on only 'half the circle' using coord_polar
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working with some rotational data, continuous data that one might
normally summarise with a boxplot.
Because it's rotational data centered on zero with a small standard
deviation, I'm wanting to plot on the circle using polar_coord()

Here's a small example:

mydata<-data.frame(Rotation = rnorm(100,sd=10),
Group=c(rep("A",50),rep("B",50)))

ggplot(mydata,aes(x=Group,y=Rotation)) + geom_boxplot() +
coord_polar(theta="y",start=pi)+
scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-180,180),breaks=c(-180,-90,0,90,180))+
scale_x_discrete(breaks=c("","A","B",""),limits=c("","A","B",""))

You'll probably note that there are a number of weaknesses associated
with display using the polar coordinate system in this way, and I'm
trying to overcome at least two.

First, is there a way to display only the top half of the circle in
the graph - because of the small standard deviation, the bottom half
of the plot is essentially redundant.

Second, is there a better way to bring the boxplot of A and B closer
together, further towards the outside of the circle? (Attempting to
overcome the illusion of more variation in the group closest to the
edge of the circle). I'm using limits here, but I suspect that's not
terribly clever.

Have been puzzling over this for a while - if you've any guidance I'd
greatly appreciate it.
thanks,
Brad
